headline: Nvidia took Jensen Huang back and the S&P 500 jumped 4.7% on Monday, but by Tuesday morning the bill arrived: HPE guided margins lower, ADI fell about 16% on its outlook, and the Fed's Williams kept a December hike fully priced.
summary: Closes here are Monday Nov 23 (the dashboard's prices_as_of is 2026-11-23, confirmed with Massive). Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday, and the stock closed up 31.5% at 165.05 on 783 million shares (Massive; Fortune; Yahoo Finance). The S&P 500 rose 4.7% and the Nasdaq Composite 6.5%, the best day for both since April 2025 (Traders and Quants; Yahoo Finance). SPY volume was 1.79 times its 50 day average but below Friday's options expiry session, and high yield bonds barely moved, so this was a strong first day, not yet a confirmed turn. Tuesday morning gave some of it back: S&P 500 futures were down about 0.5% at 5am ET, Nvidia was down about 5% premarket, HPE fell about 16% and ADI about 16% by late morning after their reports (Investing.com; CNBC; Benzinga; Quantisnow). Wednesday's PCE and GDP still decide how the Fed acts on Dec 9; futures now fully price a hike (CME FedWatch via Traders and Quants).

regime.why: Monday was a big up day on above average volume, and the VIX fell 26% to 26.62. But credit did not join, the move rested on one company's news, and Tuesday morning faded the chip leaders. A follow through day (a strong close on higher volume on day 4 or later of the rally) and a calm PCE on Wednesday would move this to mixed.

signals.title: Nvidia takes Huang back, and the market adds back a week of losses in a day
signals.since_yesterday: Monday's brief covered Washington's questions for Nvidia. Hours later the board unanimously reinstated Huang as CEO, president and director, and the stock closed up 31.5%.
signals.what_happened: Nvidia's board voted unanimously on Monday to bring Jensen Huang back as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, saying it was satisfied with his candor and ability to lead (Yahoo Finance; Fortune). The board said it met with Huang and senior government leaders; President Trump said he spoke to the board (Yahoo Finance; Fortune). NVDA closed 165.05, up 31.48%, on 783 million shares against 633 million on Friday (Massive), adding close to $1 trillion of value (Fortune). Chips followed: SMH +15.0%, MU +19.0%, TSM +14.1%, TXN +10.4%, ADI +9.5%; Taiwan's EWT +18.0% and Korea's EWY +10.1% (Massive). The S&P 500 rose 4.73% and the Nasdaq 6.51% (Yahoo Finance). The investigations go on: the SEC, FBI, Commerce and Justice departments, House and Senate committees and Nvidia's own outside counsel are still looking at the China matter (Fortune).
signals.so_what: Follow the money: the market priced Huang himself at about $1 trillion, which tells you how much of the AI build out rests on one buyer's leadership. Who gets paid: Nvidia's suppliers (TSMC, Micron, the server makers), which had been sold as if orders were at risk. Who pays: anyone who sold the panic, and the short sellers. What would make this wrong: the probes. A fine or a China sales limit is still possible, and credit markets did not rally with stocks (the main high yield ETF rose only 0.25%, Traders and Quants), so bond buyers did not see a change in the economy.
signals.for_you: Swing: no chip entries. NVDA, TSM and MU are bounces inside downtrends; NVDA has no buy point until it closes back over its falling 200 day (202.99). Puts: no chip puts; the group swings 10% to 30% a day. Long term: ENTG (on the long term scan buy list) jumped 14.1% to 142.06 and now sits 1.5% over its 139.99 point; wait for Wednesday's data before any piece.

signals.title: Tuesday's bill: HPE guides margins down, ADI drops on an in line outlook, and Williams keeps the hike alive
signals.what_happened: HPE reported fiscal Q4 revenue of $14.5 billion, up 50%, with server sales of $8.8 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.43 above estimates, but guided its cloud and AI unit's operating margin to about 14% for fiscal 2027 from 18.4% in Q4, as AI systems carry thinner margins and price increases slow (Traders and Quants). HPE traded at 40.21, down 16.3%, at 11:45am ET (Benzinga, 15 minute delayed), after closing 48.02 Monday, up 17.4% (Massive). ADI reported record Q4 revenue of $4.37 billion, up 42%, and adjusted EPS of $4.06 against a $3.86 guide; it guided Q1 to $4.4 billion and $3.82 adjusted EPS with adjusted operating margin down about 1.8 points (ADI 8-K; MLQ.ai). ADI was down 16.05% at 10:20am ET, about 317.66 (Quantisnow), its worst day since 2020 (Barron's). New York Fed President Williams said Monday that inflation near 3.5% is "simply too high," that chip prices have "increased sharply," and that he would not rule out hikes at back to back meetings; fed funds futures fully price a Dec 9 hike (Traders and Quants, citing CME FedWatch). IBD also reported hike odds jumping.
signals.so_what: Second order: Monday bought back the AI revenue story, and Tuesday showed the cost side. Memory and parts are scarce, so server makers raise prices (HPE and Dell have asked buyers to pay more on signed orders, per a Financial Times report cited by Traders and Quants), and the margin goes to whoever owns the scarce part: Micron, SK Hynix, TSMC, not the box makers. ADI's drop is about expectations: it rose 63% in a year and 9.2% Monday, then guided to a small step down. What would make this wrong: Dell tonight holding its margin while passing on higher memory costs.
signals.for_you: Swing: no entries into Dell's report tonight or PCE Wednesday. Puts: ADI is blocked. It is on the long term scan buy list as 'Buy zone now', but the intraday price is under its zone (365.84) and under the buy point stop (347.55), so do not sell ADI puts or buy ADI today, whatever the tile says. HPE is the same: its long term point (45.58) and zone low (41.42) are both above the intraday price. Long term: wait for ADI and HPE to build a new base.

signals.title: Monday's brief graded: right on the bounce and the deal, wrong on Nvidia and India
signals.since_yesterday: Monday's closes are in. Three calls held, two did not.
signals.what_happened: Graded with Massive closes for Nov 23. (1) The bounce: right in direction, far too small in size. We quoted S&P 500 futures up about 2.1% near 1:20am ET; SPY closed up 4.71% on 1.79x its 50 day volume. (2) Nvidia: wrong. We listed NVDA under 'hurt' for the Bessent story and expected the probe to weigh on it. The board reinstated Huang that morning and NVDA closed up 31.5% on heavy volume. We had no sign of the reversal at 6am, but the call was wrong. (3) CrowdStrike and Zscaler: right. CRWD closed 208.97, down 8.9%, on 42.4 million shares (3.3 times Friday's); ZS closed 229.24, up 17.7%. At 1.135 CRWD per share the deal is now worth about $237.18 per ZS share, not the $260.41 we quoted on Friday's close, and ZS trades 3.4% under it. MLQ.ai reports Deutsche Bank puts the chance of regulatory approval under 50% (one source). (4) India: wrong on the day. INDA fell 1.44% to 52.14 on 12.9 million shares, 2.0 times its 50 day average, as money ran back to US chips; it held its 52.13 breakout level by one cent. HDB fell 1.1% and IBN was flat. (5) The rate note changed: on Monday a December hike was 'no longer fully priced'; by Tuesday futures price it fully again (Traders and Quants; IBD).
signals.so_what: A heavy volume down day right after a breakout is a warning: INDA's buyers from Friday were tested at once. The dashboard has already reset INDA's buy point to a new breakout at 53.20 with a 51.87 stop. The deal spread on ZS is small for a deal with real antitrust doubt, so the market is not paying for that risk yet.
signals.for_you: Swing: INDA is a wait, not a buy, until it closes over 53.20 on 9,700,000+ shares (1.5x normal); a close under 51.87 ends the setup. Puts: no CRWD or ZS puts. Long term: no change.

signals.title: Medtronic: ablation grew 58%, revenue came in light, and Sanofi pays $41 billion for Insmed
signals.since_yesterday: Medtronic reported this morning. The numbers below are new.
signals.what_happened: Medtronic's fiscal Q2 revenue was $9.364 billion, up 4.5% reported and 6.5% organic, about 0.5 point over its own guide; non-GAAP EPS was $1.34, in line with the $1.34 consensus we cited Monday, and it kept full year guidance of 7.25% to 7.75% organic growth and $5.94 to $6.00 EPS (Medtronic 8-K via MLQ.ai). Reuters called it a revenue miss against estimates after the MiniMed split (consensus was $9.47 billion). Cardiac ablation grew 58%, with 80% US growth and 7 points of share gained; electrophysiology grew 18.5% organic; neuromodulation fell 2.2% (8-K). The stock fell about 4% early Tuesday (Investing.com); it closed 100.72 Monday (Massive). Separately, Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 a share in cash, about $41 billion, pharma's biggest deal since 2023; the premium is about 46% over the price before deal reports but about 17% over Monday's close (CNBC; Axios; Traders and Quants). IBD reported that Kymera's eczema pill showed Dupixent like results at 16 weeks; KYMR closed up 30.4% Monday (Massive). Regeneron, which sells Dupixent with Sanofi, rose 2.3%.
signals.so_what: For a clinician: pulsed field ablation is the fastest growing device market in cardiology, and Medtronic is taking share from older tools. The rest of the company grows slower, so the stock trades on the mix. Big pharma is paying up for late stage respiratory and immunology drugs as patents roll off; that keeps a bid under mid cap biotech with approved drugs. What would make this wrong: hospital capital budgets tightening in a slowing economy.
signals.for_you: Swing: MDT's pullback setup needed a close over 102.61; a 4% drop takes it back toward its 94.65 point, and its stop is 6.1% away, wider than the 6% limit. No trade. Puts: the report is out, but MDT is on the watch list, not the buy list (6.4% over its long term point at Monday's close), so no puts yet. Long term: MDT moves closer to its zone (84.56 to 97.49); watch it. No action on INSM or KYMR.

signals.title: China keeps critical metals flowing to the US until late January
signals.what_happened: China extended its pause on the gallium, germanium and antimony export ban to the US until about Jan 27, 2027, instead of letting it end on Nov 27 (Wall Street Journal; Bloomberg; BigGo Finance, Nov 24). Bloomberg framed it as keeping the trade truce with the US intact.
signals.so_what: The deadline we have tracked on the critical materials map since early November is gone for two months. Who gets paid: US chip and defense makers that buy these metals keep their supply. Who pays: the scarcity story behind small US producers such as UAMY loses its near term deadline. Third order: a truce that holds through January lowers one risk for Asian chip stocks that just rallied.
signals.for_you: No action. MP, UAMY and USAR still have no buy point (lower highs and lower lows). The next date is late January.

cycle.quadrant: Growth slowing while inflation stays high: late overheating, leaning toward stagflation
cycle.quadrant_why: New York Fed President Williams put inflation near 3.5% and said he does not expect 2% until 2028, naming energy and AI chip prices as the shocks still running (Traders and Quants, Nov 24). Wednesday's PCE and GDP are the next test. The All Weather model is not changed.
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Tightening and late. A December hike went from 'no longer fully priced' on Friday to fully priced by Tuesday (CME FedWatch via Traders and Quants), and Williams would not rule out hikes at back to back meetings.
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. The White House pressing a company's board to rehire its CEO, a day after the Treasury Secretary pressed the Fed, shows how much the government now leans on asset prices.
cycle.big_cycle: Internal order: political pressure on a private board decided the market's biggest move. Technology: AI demand is now raising prices for chips and memory, which the Fed counts as inflation. External order: China extended the metals truce to late January.
tailwinds: Nvidia's leadership risk is off the table for now, and Asian chip markets followed (Taiwan's Taiex +9.0% Tuesday, Traders and Quants).
China's metals pause runs to about Jan 27.
Brent closed at $89.37, its lowest since late August.
headwinds: A December hike is fully priced, and AI chip prices are now part of the inflation case.
Credit did not confirm Monday's rally, and Tuesday faded the chip leaders.

history.what: Two of the largest one day S&P 500 gains: +11.6% on Oct 13, 2008 and +9.4% on Mar 24, 2020. The 2008 jump came five months before the low (March 2009); the 2020 jump came one day after the low.
history.lesson: A huge up day does not tell you which kind of bounce it is. What followed did: in 2020 the Fed was cutting and buyers came back day after day; in 2008 credit kept breaking.

cycle.differences: Unlike 2020, the Fed is set to hike, not cut. Unlike 2008, credit is calm rather than breaking; it simply did not rally. The trigger was one company's leadership, not policy.
cycle.for_you: Swing: wait for a follow through day, not a single surge. Puts: richer premiums but no liquid contract passed today. Long term: small pieces only after Wednesday's data, and only in names still inside their zones.
